qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Core deposit franchise scale (~$1.4T deposits across ~4,000 branches) creates low-cost funding advantages and high account switching costs. Proof: 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 13.64% and ROTCE of 14.6%-16.3%. Primary erosion threats stem from fintech digital payment rails, neobank deposit competition, and regulatory compliance burdens.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Fortress Balance Sheet, REJECT). While CEO Charlie Scharf has successfully overhauled compliance and governance—leading to the Federal Reserve lifting the $1.95T asset cap in June 2025 and terminating remaining consent orders—Wells Fargo remains a fractional-reserve commercial deposit bank with ~11.5x asset leverage ($2.1T+ in assets on ~$181B in equity). Its balance sheet inherently depends on short-term deposits and wholesale liquidity subject to duration mismatch and credit cycles (the 'kindness of strangers'), structurally failing the Munger fortress balance sheet standard (g6_default: N).
qualitative.evidence: Wells Fargo is a 'Big Four' US diversified bank with ~$1.4T in deposits and ~4,000 branches. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 13.64% with ROTCE expanding to 16.3% by 2026. The Federal Reserve officially lifted the $1.95T asset cap on June 3, 2025 following extensive risk management overhaul. However, under Gate 6 criteria, commercial fractional-reserve deposit banks are disqualified by default: balance sheet leverage is ~11.5x ($2.1T+ assets vs. $181B equity), multi-year free cash flow conversion is distorted/negative (-2.3%) due to deposit and loan flows, and solvency relies on regulatory lender-of-last-resort mechanisms rather than an unleveraged, independent fortress balance sheet.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
